title: Efficient Energy-Constrained Semi-Device-Independent QRNG with an Integrated Heterodyne Receiver
authors: Mattia Sabatini, Carles Roch i Carceller, Tommaso Bertapelle, Andrea Peri, Giulio Gualandi, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Yoann Piétri, Giacomo Corrielli, Paolo Villoresi, Giuseppe Vallone, Roberto Osellame, Armin Tavakoli, Marco Avesani
abstract: Semi-device-independent QRNG frameworks represent a particularly attractive approach, combining strong security guarantees with high randomness generation rates while relying only on reduced and practical physical assumptions. A recently proposed approach based on photon-number constraints is particularly suited to photonic implementations, where these assumptions can be easily assessed experimentally. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a quantum random number generator within this framework, enabling the direct computation of lower bounds on the certifiable Shannon entropy via semidefinite relaxation techniques. When combined with entropy accumulation methods, this approach enables finite-size randomness certification without assuming independent and identically distributed rounds. We realize the protocol using a four-state coherent-state constellation symmetrically distributed in phase space and measured by heterodyne detection, certifying 0.223 bit per measurement, which is the highest value reported to date for a continuous-variable semi-device-independent QRNG. The implementation combines a low-loss integrated photonic heterodyne receiver with a simple transmitter assembled from commercial components, providing a practical and high-speed architecture for semi-device-independent randomness generation.
summary: The paper presents an experimental Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) utilizing continuous variables and QPSK modulation. It achieves state-of-the-art randomness certification by employing advanced mathematical tools like Semidefinite Programming to bound the conditional Shannon entropy in a semi-device-independent setting. This work is significant for realizing high-speed, provably secure quantum random number sources.
main_problem: Developing a Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) framework that provides strong security guarantees while maintaining high randomness generation rates using practical physical assumptions.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a QRNG achieving 0.223 bits per measurement, setting a record for continuous-variable semi-device-independent QRNGs, and reaching a rate of 55.6 Mbit/s.
method: Randomness certification is achieved by bounding the conditional Shannon entropy using Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations, which are extended to handle non-i.i.d. finite-size regimes via Entropy Accumulation Theorems.
model_or_system: The protocol uses a prepare-and-measure scheme with four-state coherent-state constellations (QPSK modulation), measured by a low-loss integrated photonic heterodyne receiver.
key_observables: Certified Shannon entropy per measurement, observable witness value $W$, and the vacuum component bound $\omega$.
important_parameters: The achieved rate is 55.6 Mbit/s at 250 Mbaud; the efficiency ($\eta$) is estimated around 0.38.
main_assumptions: The security relies on a Semi-Device-Independent (SDI) framework, assuming bounds on the average vacuum component and observable correlations ($W$ and $\omega$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate state distributions in phase space, schematics of the experimental setup, and comparisons of certifiable randomness bounds versus mean photon number $|\alpha|^2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for robust SDI frameworks to detailing the mathematical machinery (SDP relaxations) used for entropy bounding, culminating in an experimental demonstration using integrated photonics.
why_interesting: This work bridges advanced quantum information theory (SDP bounds on entropy) with cutting-edge photonic hardware implementation, providing a tangible, high-performance realization of fundamental security principles.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Prepare-and-measure protocol. A device pre- pares a coherent state according to the input x ∈{0, 1, 2, 3}. This state is sent to a second device that performs a hetero- dyne measurement with outcome b ∈{0, 1, 2, 3} correspond- ing to the four quadrants in phase-space.

FIG. 2. Experimental QRNG scheme. The figure details the schematic of the device. The source’s light is split by a 99:1 BS generating both the LO and the QPSK quantum signal |α⟩after passing through a phase encoder. These are then coupled at the inputs of an optical heterodyne receiver and converted into electrical signals by a pair BPDs measuring both orthogonal quadratures of the quantum signal. PC: polarization controller, PBS: polarizing beam splitter, BS: beam splitter, PM: power meter, FPGA: field-programmable gate array, VOA: variable optical attenuator, BPD: balanced photodetector, ∆L: optical delay line, PIC: photonic integrated circuit.

FIG. 3. Conditional probabilities estimation. Esti- mated conditional probabilities p(b|x) as a function of the mean photon number |α|2 of the QPSK-modulated coherent states. For each value of |α|2, the probabilities are obtained by averaging over the four QPSK input symbols and group- ing the outcomes according to whether Bob’s detected quad- rant is the correct quadrant (same quadrant as the prepared symbol), the opposite quadrant, or one of the two neighbor- ing quadrants. The values are averaged over 50 independent acquisitions, each containing approximately one million sym- bols. Error bars account for statistical and optical-power un- certainties. FIG. 4. Certifiable randomness. The figure details the amount of randomness that can be experimentally certified per measurement: the Shannon entropy values are shown in blue, their finite-size correction obtained via the EAT framework in purple, and the min-entropy in black. The figure also includes the theoretical performance of the QRNG, with solid curves indicating the ideal case (no losses) and dashed curves representing the predictions when losses are considered.
